findings.title: Inaccurate VfsError em-dash justification
findings.location: requirements.md Out of Scope bullet; design.md 'Optional MessageId on thiserror enums'
findings.problem: Both docs assert VfsError and CommandError carry pre-existing non-ASCII em-dashes in their #[error(...)] strings. Verified against source: only CommandError (InvalidId, HistoryIo) does; VfsError's #[error(...)] strings are plain ASCII. The scope decision (leave both untouched) is correct, but the stated justification is factually wrong for VfsError.
findings.fix: Narrow the parenthetical to CommandError only (variants InvalidId and HistoryIo). Do not change the scope decision.

findings.title: MessageArgs Send+Sync asserted, could read as an explicit derive
findings.problem: The claim that MessageArgs is Clone + Send + Sync is correct, but MessageArgs derives only Debug, Default, Clone; Send + Sync are auto-traits inferred from its owned String/f64 fields. A reader could misread the text as claiming an explicit derive.
findings.fix: Clarify that Send + Sync are auto-derived (auto-traits) from the owned fields, not an explicit derive, and that StructuredMessage gets them automatically.

findings.title: MessageClass::new_static framed as 'infallible' but returns Result, and is untasked
findings.problem: The prose calls new_static 'an infallible ... path' in the same sentence that says it returns Result (self-contradictory). It is also not referenced by any task (tasks 3.1/3.2 only cover try_new), so its in-scope status is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Prefer dropping new_static for this gate (nothing needs it). If kept, remove the word 'infallible', frame it as a &'static str convenience constructor that still validates and returns Result, and add a sub-note to task 3.2 that it is implemented and tested.
